'''Edward Charles''' "'''Ted'''" '''Titchmarsh''' (June 1, 1899 – January 18, 1963) was a leading British mathematician.<ref name="frs"/><ref name="mathgene">{{mathgenealogy|name=Edward Charles Titchmarsh|id=18580}}</ref><ref name="mactutor">{{MacTutor Biography|id=Titchmarsh}}</ref>

==Education==
Titchmarsh was educated at [[King Edward VII School (Sheffield)]] and [[Balliol College, Oxford]], where he began his studies in October 1917.

==Career==
Titchmarsh was known for work in [[analytic number theory]], [[Fourier analysis]] and other parts of [[mathematical analysis]]. He wrote several classic books in these areas; his book on the [[Riemann zeta-function]] was reissued in a 1986 edition edited by [[Roger Heath-Brown]].

Titchmarsh was [[Savilian Professor of Geometry]] at the [[University of Oxford]] from 1932 to 1963. He was a Plenary Speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] in 1954 in Amsterdam.

He was on the governing body of [[Abingdon School]] from 1935-1947.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.abingdon.org.uk/uploads/school/files/abingdonian/1935_January_V007_N013.pdf#page=1|title=School Notes|publisher=The Abingdonian}}</ref>

==Awards==
*[[Fellow of the Royal Society]], 1931<ref name="frs"/>
*[[De Morgan Medal]], 1953
*[[Sylvester Medal]], 1955
*[[Berwick Prize]] winner, 1956
